subject: Clarify commit flexibility and tiered rebate eligibility for hosted API

Subject: Hosted API - baseline commit and rebate questions

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Procurement asked me to follow up with a few concrete questions so we can evaluate the hosted API pricing in our RFP. High level: we plan to pilot a customer-facing summarization feature (clinical discharge notes) and expect some seasonality. A few specific items they want clarity on:

- Do you require a minimum monthly committed spend for the hosted API (not Dedicated)? If so, how is that structured (monthly bands vs. annualized commit)?
- If usage varies month-to-month, is there a quarterly or annual true-up so we don't overpay during low months?
- Can we increase a commit mid-term and have the higher tier retroactively apply for a rebate or credit?
- How do you handle unused committed dollars? Do credits roll forward, expire, or convert to overage discounts?

Attached our short RFP excerpt for context. Happy to hop on a call if it's easier to walk through the scenarios.

Thanks,
Sonia

Hi Sonia — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together the short answers below and attached our most recent hosted rate card (Redwood-Hosted-Rate-Card-v2.pdf) plus a draft SOW outline that maps to the pilot you described.

Quick answers (summary):
- Minimum commit: We offer tiered monthly commit bands for hosted (no Dedicated required). Typical entry band starts at $10k/month; higher bands (e.g., $30k/mo, $75k/mo) get progressively larger unit discounts. We can structure as monthly recurring commits with a 12-month agreement or as an annualized commit billed monthly.
- Seasonality / true-up: We support quarterly and annual true-ups. You can opt for quarterly true-up if you expect short-term fluctuations; annual true-ups are common for customers who prefer predictability. True-up means if your actual usage exceeds the committed baseline over the true-up period, we apply a rebate/credit or invoice the overage at the agreed overage rate, whichever you prefer.
- Mid-term increases: Yes — you can increase the commit mid-term. When you move to a higher band we can apply the higher band pricing retroactively for that true-up period (i.e., you receive a credit for the period's usage that would have qualified under the higher band). This is handled as a pro-rated credit on the next invoice.
- Unused committed dollars: We offer a 30-day rollover window for unused committed spend to accommodate short dips. Unused credits beyond the rollover expire unless covered under an annual true-up where excess annual usage can offset earlier low months. We don't convert unused commit to refunds; it's structured as service credit.

A few open items I want to confirm with you on our call:
- Which commit cadence do you prefer (monthly billed vs. annualized billed monthly)?
- Do you want quarterly or annual true-up?
- Expected average monthly token/text volume and anticipated peak multipliers (helps pick the right band).

I've CC'd Aditya (solutions) to help prepare a usage projection table for the call. If you're available tomorrow afternoon, Aditya and I can join a 30-min slot to run scenarios.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Arjun / Sonia — thanks for the fast reply. Per your asks we've put together the short SOW and a three-scenario pricing summary (attached: SOW-draft-BLH.docx). Highlights below so procurement has the key terms up front: 

- Term & commit mechanics: 12-month minimum term. Commits are monthly recurring amounts; customer may elect to annualize (bill monthly) for predictable budgeting. Entry band available at $10k/month, mid band at $30k/month, and enterprise band at $75k/month. Each band includes a pre-negotiated unit price for generation tokens and embeddings; the attached rate card lists unit rates.
- True-up / rollovers: Quarterly true-up available (default) with an option to elect annual true-up. Unused committed spend rolls forward up to 30 days. For annual true-up, excess annual usage will offset earlier low months such that no committed dollars are forfeited if annual usage meets thresholds.
- Mid-term increases & retro credits: If you increase your committed band during the term, we can apply the higher-band pricing retroactively for the current true-up period (i.e., you receive a pro-rated credit on the following invoice for the period where usage would have qualified). We will document the effective date in an amendment; finance typically sees the credit applied as a line-item adjustment.
- SLA & data handling: SLA credit language is in section 5 of the draft SOW. We also attached our SOC 2 summary appendix (embedded in the SOW document). If you need the full SOC 2 report or a redaction for audit, we can start the NDA/secure-share process.
- Early termination: 60-day termination notice after the initial 12-month term with a standard early-termination fee equal to two months' committed spend if ending before term completion.

Next steps I propose: 1) Aditya will create the three-scenario usage table and share a short spreadsheet by end of day; 2) we schedule a 30-min call tomorrow at 2:30pm PT to walk the SOW and pricing; 3) if procurement is comfortable, we’ll issue a DocuSign envelope with the SOW and a one-page MSA amendment for the commit terms.
